Ok, so you know that mistakes have occurred to get you into the situation you're in. I'm not blaming you, I made my own to get homeless myself. No sense in harping on them though I do want to point out a glaring one to try and keep you from doing it again:

You took on a liability in Partially buying that car. Stop making a payment and they're going to (further) ruin your credit at best, and at worst they will find and repo the car leaving you with nothing to show for it. Don't saddle yourself with liabilities, it'll only make things more difficult. That $2k could have been 3~4 months worth of a solid roof over your head if you rented a room in a shared house. Heck, around me in GA (since you're in the SE somewhere), that would have rented you a whole house for 2 months.

Since you sound like you have a job, it's all just a numbers game. Eliminate every bill possible, including your cell service (or the data plan if you must have a phone for work). Don't worry about bank fees or other past-due bills. This is going to fuck up your credit rating, but that's a problem for another day as you're not going to be applying for loans anytime soon.

Find a real place to live. I've done the car thing (mine was a disabled Jeep with a futon in the back, it was eventually towed), it sucks and the ~$300/month for a warm room to sleep, bathroom to clean yourself and kitchen to make food at home is the best possible money spent. I haven't looked for rooms to share in my small town but I'm certain they exist. Everyone's feeling the $$$ crunch and having a rent/mortgage eased by sharing a house is an easy solution.

If you're spending money eating out and have a place to make food, that's a way to save money too. You're going to be sick of beans and rice in short order, but they are Stupid cheap but filling. I was living on about $40/month worth of groceries.

I was scrimping and saving every last cent I could so I had means to keep going if the job should evaporate, which a couple of them did.

There are also state resources to help you out. I was too prideful to ask, but it would have made a huge difference. Lots of Gov assist down here in the SE, they just about throw it at people.

Get yourself shelter and food and it's mostly a waiting game... waiting for a better job opportunity (if college wasn't your thing, look into apprenticing with a plumber, electrician or local builders ~ you'll gain skills that will allow you to make money Anywhere, and if you stick with it you can make good money with zero formal education), waiting for a cheaper/better place to live, working on building a better diet to fit your budget.

Eventually, if you want it bad enough, you'll dig yourself out of the hole. The you'll have to worry about the bills you didn't pay, credit cards and bank over-draft fees, etc... It's just another game of getting a loan (I bought a car, could have paid cash but instead paid that cash to a bank for a secured loan, they put it in a CD incase I defaulted, that one positive loan on my credit all but erased the negatives ~ it took me 8 years to get to that point though).

Good luck. Don't be afraid to ask for help as a Lot of people have been through what you're going through. Lots of ways to get out of it, but also just as many ways to stay in that shitty place.
